plain_english: Never say you've "lost" something. Say you've "returned" it. Did your child die? You returned them. Did your wife die? You returned her. Did someone take your property? You returned that too. "But the person who took it was evil." What does that matter? The one who gave it to you took it back through whatever means. While you have something, treat it like it's not really yours. Think of yourself as a traveler staying at an inn.
original_excerpt: Never say of anything, “I have lost it,” but, “I have restored it.” Has your child died? It is restored. Has your wife died? She is restored. Has your estate been taken away? That likewise is restored. “But it was a bad man who took it.” What is it to you by whose hands he who gave it has demanded it again? While he permits you to possess it, hold it as something not your own, as do travelers at an inn.
